newsitem.title: USA: "First Wives Club" maintains box office lead.
newsitem.headline: "First Wives Club" maintains box office lead.

text.p: "The First Wives Club" enjoyed a healthy lead over its box office rivals for the second consecutive weekend, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
The comedy starring Bette Midler, Goldie Hawn and Diane Keaton as vengeful ex-wives, earned $15.5 million for the Friday to Sunday period, said Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.

Thanks to the addition of almost 400 screens this weekend, the film's weekend take fell by just 18 percent. Its 10-day total is $42.0 million, and industry analysts expect the movie to end up with more than $100 million domestically.

Opening in a distant second was the Hugh Grant medical thriller "Extreme Measures", which took in $7.1 million. Grant plays a physician who stumbles across a scheme involving experimentation on unsuspecting patients.

The movie, which was produced by his girlfriend Liz Hurley, is released by Sony Corp's Columbia Pictures. Its screen average of $3,090 indicates it will perform modestly at the box office. Reviewers were almost evenly divided: a Variety poll of critics in New York, Los Angeles, Washington DC and Chicago showed that 15 liked it, 16 did not and 16 were mixed.

The critically mauled Bruce Willis gangster movie "Last Man Standing" slipped a notch to third in its second weekend with $4.1 million. Its 10-day total is $13.2 million. The movie is released by New Line Cinema, a unit of Turner Broadcasting System Inc.
Opening in fourth was the Los Angeles-based crime saga "2 Days in the Valley", a moderate release with an ensemble cast including James Spader and Teri Hatcher.

It earned $3.48 million from 769 screens - compared to more than 2,200 screens for each of the top three - and its average of $4,525 was the highest in the top 10. Critics were reasonably favorable: 16 liked it, 11 did not and 11 were mixed. MGM, which is being bought by a consortium headed by Kirk Kerkorian, released the movie.
Columbia Pictures' "Fly Away Home" fell two places to fifth in its third weekend with $3.2 million. Its total is $13.5 million.
